 ..

This application coming on for orders this day, th e co  following:
 ORDER
Heard and perused the record.

(1) This is SECOND bail application filed on behalf of the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail in relation to Crime No.109/2022, dated (not mentioned),
registered at Police Station-Raoti, District-Ratlam for the offence under Sections for the offences under Sections 363,366,376(2)(n),376(3) of I.P.C, 1860 and Section 5l/6 of POCSO Act.
He is in custody since 14.06.2022.
His first application was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to file afresh after six months vide order dated 26.06.2023.
Now, after completing of the liberty granted on earlier occasion, present petition has been filed.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in this case.
The prosecutrix and the applicant resided together for a period of more than four months.
As per the statement recorded under Section 164 of CrPC, the prosectrix was a consenting party.
In this case the statement of prosecutrix has been recorded before the Trial Court.

In paragraph No. 11, she has admitted that if the applicant would have paid the money regarding Bhanjgarha, the report would not have been filed by the parents of the prosecutrix against the applicant.
The applicant is in custody since 14.06.2022.
Final conclusion of the trial will take a long time.
Under these circumstances, he prays for grant of bail to the applicant.
(3) Learned Panel lawyer for the respondent/State, on the other hand, has opposed the prayer.

(4) After hearing learned counsel for the parties and looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, as well as the custody period, I am of the view that it is a case, in which applicant may be released on bail.
Consequently without commenting on the merits of the case, bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

(5) It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
(6) This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case o f bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(PREM NARAYAN SINGH) JUDGE VD Dilip Charel vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8476495/
